title: Patient Care Desk Guidance: Repeated Short Fills on Non-Controlled Prescriptions
content:
A Kestrel Prescriptions record in the Non-Controlled Acute Prescription, Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription or Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription class that has been dispensed short again and again earns a non-controlled recovery amount when the patient declines its owed balance.

## The rule the desk applies

The non-controlled recovery amount counts the owed-balance entries booked on the prescription in the last 12 months:

- **three or more** add **2.00**;
- **exactly two** add **1.00**;
- **one** adds nothing.

The recovery amount is added to the non-controlled decline credit.

## Reading the fill ledger (hypothetical histories)

| Owed-balance entries on the prescription in the last 12 months (the declined one included) | Recovery amount |
|---|---|
| 1 | nothing |
| 2 | 1.00 |
| 3 | 2.00 |
| 5 | 2.00 |

**An owed-balance entry from 14 months ago.** It falls outside the last 12 months and is not counted.

**Does an owed balance that was completed still count?** Yes; the count is of owed-balance entries booked on the prescription in the last 12 months, however each was later settled.
